reason: The primary user-facing purpose is providing an interactive terminal experience within the DSH web interface: it opens a floating, session-local REPL window and executes JavaScript through a host-process `node:repl` session. Evidence in the README and package metadata consistently points to terminal UI + websocket bridge behavior rather than search, file editing, or knowledge-management features. Because execution is in-process and linked to live agent context, its capability is terminal/tooling oriented but with high-impact local effects.

summaries.zh: 这是一个面向会话的 DSH 网页终端插件，可在会话内打开浮动 Node.js REPL，直接运行代码并在同一会话中使用运行时上下文。
summaries.en: This plugin adds a per-session floating Node.js terminal in the DSH web UI so users can run JavaScript in a live REPL with session runtime context.

capabilities: Per-session interactive Node.js REPL execution in the browser UI
WebSocket bridge to a backend node:repl process
Direct access to live runtime context objects (`ctx`/`agent`) from the REPL
Session-scoped terminal window lifecycle controls (open, collapse, close)

reasons.code: The plugin is documented as a per-session floating Node REPL terminal in the DSH web UI, with session-local controls and lifecycle behavior.
The REPL is described as an in-process `node:repl` instance with live agent context (`ctx`, `agent`) in scope.
Package metadata includes terminal/WebSocket tooling (`node-pty`, `ws`) and web client injection for DSH, matching a terminal bridge implementation.
Repository description and README explicitly state the REPL runs inside the host process and is unsandboxed.
